artifacts.summary: Wrapped Expressiveness/README.md and WeakCanonical/README.md in cols=files-lines generated-inventory blocks, with the two Kamp rollup tables recorded as a deliberate reasoned exclusion.

completion_data.completion_summary: Wrapped FormalSystem/Metalogic/Expressiveness/README.md and FormalSystem/Metalogic/WeakCanonical/README.md in cols=files-lines generated-inventory blocks (4-column Module|Files|Lines|Description), with every subdirectory total now machine-owned and every hand-written description preserved except the 10 deliberately stripped (N files) parentheticals. Verified via key-sorted before/after diffs and an independent corrupt/restore demonstration per file. The two Kamp rollup tables were left unwrapped and the reason recorded in the task summary as a deliberate, reasoned exclusion (no generator option reproduces their loose-modules aggregate-row shape without extending the generator, which is out of scope).

memory_candidates.content: scripts/check-module-invariants.sh's cols=files-lines option, when applied to a directory-rollup inventory table, renders every subdirectory row as two real integers (file count, line total) instead of the cols=lines default's '-' placeholder, and renders every loose-file row with a literal '1' prepended as its file count. The header is NEVER derived from cols= -- render_block() carries the existing table's first row-shaped line forward verbatim -- so converting a 3-column File|Lines|Description table to 4-column Module|Files|Lines|Description requires a one-time hand rewrite of the header and separator lines before the first --emit-inventory run. Neither rows=subdirs (silently drops a 'loose modules' aggregate row with no per-row concept for it) nor rows=both (explodes that one row into one per loose file) reproduces a hand-maintained rollup table whose loose files are summarized in a single aggregate row -- that shape has no existing marker-option combination and requires a new generator option to cover.

When a corrupt/restore demonstration is used to prove a generated-content gate's coverage, restore via the generator's own writer mode (e.g. --emit-inventory), never via a pathspec checkout (git checkout -- <path> / git restore <path>) -- both are blocked destructive forms on a dirty tree under this repo's guard-destructive-git.sh hook, and the writer restores a generated block to its canonical content by construction, which is also the more honest proof: it demonstrates the SAME mechanism that will fix a real future drift, not an unrelated git-level revert.
